object.title: Linear chemical distances in scale-free Gilbert graphs
object.statement: Let $G(X^{(n)})$ be the scale-free Gilbert graph on the point set $X^{(n)}$ in the torus $\mathbb{T}_n$, let $\mathsf{e}_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)$, and let $q(x)$ denote the closest point of $X$ to $x$. Assume $s>d$. **Linear chemical-distance conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(\beta,d)>0$ such that the chemical distance between $q(-n\mathsf{e}_1/4)$ and $q(n\mathsf{e}_1/4)$ is at least $cn$ with high probability as $n\to\infty$. The preceding theorem proves only a lower bound of order $n/(\log n)^{\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$; the conjecture asserts that this sublogarithmic loss is an artifact of the proof and that distances are instead bounded below linearly.
object.source_name: Christian Hirsch, “From heavy-tailed Boolean models to scale-free Gilbert graphs”, arXiv:1411.6824 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6824

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

object.title: Zauner's conjecture on maximal complex equiangular tight frames
object.statement: Let $M\geq 2$. An equiangular tight frame (ETF) in $\mathbb{C}^M$ with $N$ vectors is denoted by $\operatorname{ETF}(M,N)$; the maximal possible number of vectors in the complex case is $N=M^2$. **Zauner's conjecture.** There exists an equiangular tight frame $\operatorname{ETF}(M,M^2)$ for every $M\geq 2$. These maximal ETFs are also called symmetric, informationally complete, positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs) and are important in quantum Bayesianism, quantum state tomography, and quantum cryptography. Their existence is conjectured in every dimension, but the general existence question remains open.
object.source_name: Matthew Fickus and Dustin G. Mixon, “Tables of the existence of equiangular tight frames”, arXiv:1504.00253 (2016).

object.title: Sublinear-distance conjecture for three to six longest paths
object.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, let $\mathcal{L}(G)$ denote the set of longest paths of $G$, and let $f(G,\mathcal{P})$ denote the distance parameter for a subset $\mathcal{P}$ of longest paths. A function $g$ is **sublinear** if $g(n)/n\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$. **Sublinear-distance conjecture.** There exists a sublinear function $g$ such that for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$ and every subset $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathcal{L}(G)$ with $3\leq |\mathcal{P}|\leq 6$, $f(G,\mathcal{P})\leq g(n)$. The source states that this conjecture is equivalent to the common-vertex conjecture for three through six longest paths; it is not resolved in the paper.
object.source_name: Jan Ekstein, Shinya Fujita, Adam Kabela and Jakub Teska, “Bounding the distance among longest paths in a connected graph”, arXiv:1607.08850 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.08850

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

object.title: Cubic-root-of-three lower-bound conjecture for cycles in graphs
object.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $C(G)$ denote the number of cycles in a graph $G$. **Cubic-root-of-three lower-bound conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $m$, there exists a graph $G$ with $m$ edges and at least

$$
(1+o(1))^m(\sqrt[3]{3})^m
$$

cycles.

The conjecture proposes that the exponential growth rate supplied by the paper's multigraph construction is also achievable, up to a subexponential factor, by simple graphs. The source gives no resolution of this claim.
object.source_name: Andrii Arman and Sergei Tsaturian, “The maximum number of cycles in a graph with fixed number of edges”, arXiv:1702.02662 (2017).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

object.title: Chen–Lev strengthened conjecture on explicit Hilbert-cube pairs
object.statement:
Let $C$ and $D$ be different sets of nonnegative integers satisfying

$$
C\cup D=\mathbb N,
$$

$$
C\cap D=r+m\mathbb N,
$$

for integers $r\ge0$ and $m\ge2$, and let $R_C(n)$ and $R_D(n)$ denote their two-element representation functions.

**Chen–Lev strengthened conjecture.** If $R_C(n)=R_D(n)$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists an integer $l\ge1$ such that

$$
C=H_0(1,2,4,8,\dots,2^{2l-1},2^{2l}-1,2^{2l+1}-1,2(2^{2l+1}-1),4(2^{2l+1}-1),8(2^{2l+1}-1),\dots),
$$

$$
D=H_1(1,2,4,8,\dots,2^{2l-1},2^{2l}-1,2^{2l+1}-1,2(2^{2l+1}-1),4(2^{2l+1}-1),8(2^{2l+1}-1),\dots).
$$

This is explicitly described as a stronger version of the Chen–Lev question and would identify the sets themselves, not only the parameters of their periodic intersection. The source supplies no resolution.
object.source_name: Sándor Z. Kiss and Csaba Sándor, “On the structure of sets which have coinciding representation functions”, arXiv:1702.04499 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.04499

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

object.title: The maximal-energy-concentration obstruction to Poissonian pair correlations
object.statement: Let $(a(n))_{n\geq1}$ be the sequence of integers used to form $A_N=\{a(1),\ldots,a(N)\}$, and let $E(A_N)$ denote its additive energy. For a real number $\alpha$, consider the sequence $(\{a(n)\alpha\})_{n\geq1}$ on the torus. **Pair-correlation obstruction conjecture.** If $E(A_N)=\Omega(N^3)$, then there is no $\alpha$ for which the pair correlations of $(\{a(n)\alpha\})_{n\geq1}$ are Poissonian. This strengthens the known result that non-Poissonian pair correlations occur for every $\alpha$ in a positive-measure subset of $[0,1]$.
object.source_name: Ida Aichinger, Christoph Aistleitner and Gerhard Larcher, “On Quasi-Energy-Spectra, Pair Correlations of Sequences and Additive Combinatorics”, arXiv:1708.08590 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08590

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2017). “Here the word ``generic'' is a bit vague; it essentially means that one excludes the known obvious (and less obvious) counterexamples to the conjecture.”

object.title: Constant-error rainbow tree embedding conjecture
object.statement:
A **properly coloured** graph is an edge-coloured graph in which edges sharing a vertex have distinct colours. A subgraph is **rainbow** if all its edges have distinct colours. Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices.

**Constant-error rainbow tree conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that every properly coloured $K_n$ has a rainbow copy of every tree on $n-C$ vertices.

The paper proves rainbow copies for every tree on $n-o(n)$ vertices and explains that the error term cannot be zero. The conjecture asks whether the error can be reduced to a constant.
object.source_name: Richard Montgomery, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Embedding rainbow trees with applications to graph labelling and decomposition”, arXiv:1803.03316 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2018).

object.title: The weak acyclic matching conjecture for cyclic groups of prime order
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group. It has the **weak acyclic matching property** if, for every pair of finite subsets $A$ and $B$ of $G$ with $\#A=\#B$ and $A\cap(A+B)=\emptyset$, there is at least one acyclic matching from $A$ to $B$.

**Weak acyclic matching conjecture.** There exists a prime $p$ such that $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ does not satisfy the weak acyclic matching property.

This is a weaker property than the acyclic matching property because the condition $A\cap(A+B)=\emptyset$ ensures that every bijection from $A$ to $B$ is a matching. The paper notes that infinitely many prime cyclic groups fail the acyclic matching property, but whether one fails the weak version remains open.
object.source_name: Mohsen Aliabadi and Mano Vikash Janardhanan, “On matchable subsets in abelian groups and their linear analogues”, arXiv:1808.01376 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01376

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2018). “In what follows we provide an open problem concerning the linear acyclic matching property in field extensions.”

object.title: Odd-cycle saturation conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_{2k+1}$ denote the family consisting of the cycle $C_{2k+1}$, and let $\mathrm{sat}(\mathcal{C}_{2k+1};n)$ be its saturation number on $n$ vertices. **Odd-cycle saturation conjecture.** For all $k\ge 1$ there exists a $c_k>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{sat}(\mathcal{C}_{2k+1};n)\le \left(\frac{1}{4}-c_k\right)n^2+o(n^2).
$$

This conjecture predicts a strict improvement over the general quadratic upper bound for saturation by every odd cycle. The source presents it as an expected stronger bound; no resolution is given.
object.source_name: Sam Spiro, “Saturation Games for Odd Cycles”, arXiv:1808.03696 (2019).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

object.title: Monotone coupling conjecture for random regular graphs
object.statement:
Let $n$ be the number of vertices, and let $0\le d_1\le d_2\le n-1$ be integers such that $d_1n$ and $d_2n$ are even. Write ${\mathcal G}(n,d_i)$ for the uniformly random $d_i$-regular graph. A **coupling** $(G_1,G_2)$ is a joint realization with these marginal distributions. **Monotone coupling conjecture.** Except for $(d_1,d_2)=(1,2)$ and $(d_1,d_2)=(n-3,n-2)$, there exists a coupling $(G_1,G_2)$ such that

$$
G_1\sim {\mathcal G}(n,d_1),\qquad G_2\sim {\mathcal G}(n,d_2),
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{\mathbb P}(G_1\subseteq G_2)=1-o(1).
$$

This conjecture asks for asymptotically almost-sure containment whenever the larger regular degree is at least the smaller one. The weakened sandwich results cited in the paper do not imply this assertion, even when the degree gap is large.
object.source_name: Pu Gao, Mikhail Isaev and Brendan McKay, “Sandwiching random regular graphs between binomial random graphs”, arXiv:1906.02886 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02886

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2019). “However, the weakened versions of the sandwich conjecture, as proved in and , are not strong enough to imply the existence of such a coupling, even when $d_2$ is much greater than $d_1$.”

object.title: The planar-poset standard-example conjecture
object.statement: Let $P$ be a planar poset, let $d\ge2$, and let $S_d$ denote the standard example of order $d$. The dimension of $P$ is denoted by $\dim(P)$. **The planar-poset standard-example conjecture.** For every $d\ge2$, there exists a constant $d_0$ such that if $P$ is a planar poset and $\dim(P)\ge d_0$, then $P$ contains $S_d$ as a subposet. This is a long-standing folklore conjecture about whether planar posets of sufficiently large dimension must contain arbitrarily large standard examples; its status is presented here as open.
object.source_name: Csaba Biró, Bartłomiej Bosek, Heather C. Smith, William T. Trotter, Ruidong Wang and Stephen J. Young, “Planar Posets that are Accessible from Below Have Dimension at Most 6”, arXiv:1906.08145 (2019).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

object.title: Existence of extremal graphs for every degeneracy
object.statement:
Let $d$ be an integer with $d\geq 2$. A graph is **$d$-degenerate** if every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $d$. Let $f(H,p)$ denote the subgraph query complexity, and write $b$ for the relevant query parameter.

**Extremal graph existence conjecture.** For every integer $d\geq 2$, there exists a $d$-degenerate graph $H$ such that

$$
f(H,p)=b^{d-o(1)}.
$$

In the case $d=2$, the paper constructs such a graph, whereas the existence of such graphs for $d\geq 3$ remains open.
object.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, Chady Ben Hamida, Xiaoyu He and Alexander Moreira, “On the subgraph query problem”, arXiv:1911.04413 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04413

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “The existence of such graphs when $d\ge 3$ remains open.”

object.title: The weak Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture for one very fast speed
object.statement:
Let $n\geq4$ be an integer. For positive integers $v_1<\cdots<v_n$, define

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\min_{1\leq i\leq n}\Vert tv_i\Vert.
$$

**Weak Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq4$, there exists a function $f_n:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, whenever $v_n>f_n(v_{n-1})$, either

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\frac{s}{ns+1}\quad\text{for some }s\in\mathbb{N},
$$

or

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\geq\frac{1}{n}.
$$

This is a regime-specific refinement of the Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture, addressing sets of speeds with one speed sufficiently larger than the preceding one. The paper proves a stronger explicit bound for $n=4$ and $n=6$, but the assertion for every $n\geq4$ remains open.
object.source_name: Noah Kravitz, “Barely lonely runners and very lonely runners”, arXiv:1912.06034 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.06034

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

object.title: The conjecture that every quintic graph has at least two Kempe equivalence classes
object.statement: Let a **quintic graph** be a 5-regular graph, and let two 1-factorisations be **Kempe equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of Kempe switches. **Kempe-class conjecture.** Every quintic graph contains at least two Kempe equivalence classes. The paper proves the existence of infinitely many planar 5-connected quintic graphs with at least two Kempe equivalence classes, but the asserted statement for all quintic graphs remains open.
object.source_name: Nico Van Cleemput and Carol T. Zamfirescu, “Hamiltonian cycles and 1-factors in 5-regular graphs”, arXiv:2008.03173 (2022).

object.title: Holub–Lužar–Mihaliková–Mockovčiaková–Soták's cycle product existence conjecture
object.statement:
Let $C_m$ and $C_n$ be cycles, and let $C_m\square C_n$ denote their Cartesian product.

**Holub–Lužar–Mihaliková–Mockovčiaková–Soták's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that for every integer $m\geq c$, there is an integer $n$ satisfying

$$
\chi'_{st}(C_m\square C_n)=6.
$$

The survey states this as an equivalent formulation of the path–cycle product conjecture. Since Cartesian products of two cycles have star chromatic index between $6$ and $7$, the assertion asks for a $6$-coloring for at least one cycle length $n$ for every sufficiently large $m$.
object.source_name: Hui Lei and Yongtang Shi, “A survey on star edge-coloring of graphs”, arXiv:2009.08017 (2020).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

object.title: Langerman's chessboard mass partition conjecture
object.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers. Given a finite family of $nd$ absolutely continuous measures in $\mathds{R}^d$, a set of $n$ affine hyperplanes induces a chessboard coloring: each measure is divided according to the parity of the number of chosen positive half-spaces containing a point.

**Langerman's conjecture.** For every such family of measures, there exists a set of $n$ hyperplanes whose induced chessboard coloring splits every measure into two equal parts.

This conjecture removes directional restrictions imposed in earlier results on chessboard colorings by hyperplane arrangements. The source notes that the case $d=n=2$ was proved by Barba, Pilz, and Schnider, while the general statement remains unresolved.
object.source_name: Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, “A survey of mass partitions”, arXiv:2010.00478 (2020).
object.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Tidor's conjecture on approximately symmetric multilinear forms
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a vector space over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $alpha\colon G^k\tomathbb{F}_p$ be an $r$-approximately symmetric multilinear form, meaning that the partition rank of $alpha-\alpha\circ\pi$ is at most $r$ for every permutation $pi\in\operatorname{Sym}_k$. A multilinear form is **symmetric** if it is invariant under all permutations of its arguments. **Tidor's conjecture.** There exists a symmetric multilinear form $sigma\colon G^k\tomathbb{F}_p$ such that

$$
\operatorname{prank}(\sigma-\alpha)leq O(r^{O(1)}),
$$

where the implicit constants may depend on $p$ and $k$. Tidor formulated this conjecture in the study of the inverse problem for the Gowers uniformity norm in low characteristic and proved it for trilinear maps; the general case remains open in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Luka Milićević, “Approximately Symmetric Forms Far From Being Exactly Symmetric”, arXiv:2112.14755 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14755

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

object.title: Milićević's bounded-diameter conjecture for monochromatic component covers
object.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. An $r$-edge-coloured complete graph is a complete graph whose edges receive one of $r$ colours, and the diameter of a component is measured in its monochromatic subgraph.

**Milićević's conjecture.** For every $r$, there is a constant $D(r)$ such that every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be covered by $r-1$ monochromatic components of diameter at most $D(r)$.

This strengthens the complete-graph case of Ryser's conjecture. The source reports that it is proved for $r\leq 4$, with bounds $D(3)\leq 4$ and $D(4)\leq 6$, while the general case remains open.
object.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Bounded diameter monochromatic component covers”, arXiv:2507.05842 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2009.07239](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07239).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

object.title: Alon's star-forest extremal-graph conjecture
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a **star forest**, meaning a vertex-disjoint union of stars. For a graph $G$, let $N(G,H)$ be the number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $H$, and let

$$
N(m,H)=\max\{N(G,H):e(G)=m\}.
$$

**Alon's star-forest extremal-graph conjecture.** For every integer $m>0$, or at least for all sufficiently large $m$, there exists a star forest $G_m$ with $e(G_m)=m$ such that

$$
N(m,H)=N(G_m,H).
$$

The conjecture describes the form of an extremal graph for counting a fixed star forest with a prescribed number of edges. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so whether the assertion holds for every $m$ or only eventually remains open.
object.source_name: Peiru Kuang, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang and Jiasheng Zeng, “Proofs of Two Conjectures of Alon on Subgraph Counts”, arXiv:2606.18321 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1601.01211](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01211).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18321

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

object.title: Polynomial chi-boundedness conjecture for path-free graphs
object.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number and let $\omega(G)$ denote its clique number. A graph is **$P$-free** if it contains no induced copy of the path $P$. **Path-free polynomial chi-boundedness conjecture.** For every integer $k$, there is a constant $C_k>0$ such that every graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\geq \omega(G)^{C_k}
$$

contains an induced path of length $k$. Equivalently, for every fixed path, the class of graphs excluding that path as an induced subgraph is polynomially chi-bounded. The general chi-boundedness of path-free classes is known only in limited cases; the paper notes a bound for $P_5$-free graphs, while the stated polynomial form remains open.
object.source_name: António Girão and Zach Hunter, “Induced subdivisions in K_s,s-free graphs with polynomial average degree”, arXiv:2310.18452 (2024).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2003.12960](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12960).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
